To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SDN is not a technology, but rather a set of principles and a paradigm that is implemented through technologies.
SDN is not an architecture, but a concept that can be applied to different architectures.

SDN can be described as a layered architecture, with a clear separation between data plane and control plane, and that this architecture has three layers: the infrastructure layer, the control layer, and the application layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects of SDN: (i) What is an SDN architecture?
the development of a new network architecture that is based on a clean separation between control and data planes.
the design and implementation of a new generation of software-defined networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDN is a network architecture where the control plane and the data plane are separated by an interface or multiple interfaces or layers.
SDN is an approach to network control and management that decouples the where and how of data transmission from circuit, packet or bit string, from the management of the network.
SDN is a new approach to network programmability that is based on the separation of the control plane and the data plane and that uses an abstraction for the latter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have defined the layers of an SDN architecture and the interfaces between them.
this document provides a reference for the research community on the terminology and architecture of SDN.
this document provides an architectural view on the SDN layer structure and the terminology used to describe SDN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SDN is not a new technology, but a new approach to networking that is based on the separation of data and control planes.
there is no consensus in the research community regarding the exact definition of the SDN layers.
SDN has three layers: the application, the control and the infrastructure layer.
